findings.reason: a node implementing §4 without that reconciliation either duplicates the existing per-card-count mechanism or ships two launch axes with undefined precedence, and the plan's own "every existing invocation is unchanged" claim cannot be tested.
findings.text: §4 states that `agent serve` and `agent restart` "have no way to choose among a profile's topologies today" and adds a new `--topology <name>` axis, but `ModelProfile.gpu_variants` (imas_ambix/agent/profile.py:430) with `for_gpus` (profile.py:432) already carries per-card-count configuration overrides for one profile, and it is reached on both the serve and restart paths through `_scale_profile` (imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:248, called at cli.py:606 and cli.py:2344). Two of §4's three configurations (`b300-8x`, `b300-4x`) are keyed on the card count, which is exactly what that existing mechanism keys on, and §4 does not say whether `--topology` is built on top of `gpu_variants` or beside it, nor which wins when a launch carries both `--topology` and `--gpus` (which rescales tensor-parallel width inside whatever variant it resolved)

findings.reason: the default is the one degree of freedom the byte-identical and unchanged-invocation bullets both hinge on, and choosing it wrongly ships a launch that fails on arrival day, so the plan should state it.
findings.text: §4 says the new option's "default is the profile's default topology, so every existing invocation is unchanged", and the table row above it labels `b300-8x` "The default from day one", but no line of §4 names which of the three topologies the profile's own default is; a node that reads "default from day one" as making `b300-8x` the profile default would change what a bare `agent serve deepseek-v4-1-flash` launches (an 8-card B300 serve on a host whose name, partition and reservation are unknown until the `b300-arrival-facts` answer), which is the opposite of the unchanged-invocation bullet it also has to satisfy

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `serving-capacity-and-b300-projection` resolves as `.html` and its §6 table does carry the like-for-like column the plan quotes (1017 2,300–3,600; GLM-5.3 600–1,400; MiMo-V2.6-Pro 900–1,800; Kimi K3 800–1,500), `question b300-arrival-facts` exists, `serving-across-servers` §3 is `done` and §7 `implementable`, `rotate-to-deepseek-v4-1-flash-1017` §2/§3/§5 exist, `_preferred_owner`, `imas_ambix/agent/{cli,profile,slurm}.py` all resolve, and §2's positive control was checked against the store itself (see below).
rubric_items.done_when: a finding — §4's done-when rests on which topology is the profile's default, and the plan never names it.
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — §2–§5 write to `docs/research/*.html` and `docs/figures/...` under the repository, and §6's hour-long measures read the router's own durable request records and outcomes line, not a scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — `--topology` and the topology names `h200-4x`/`b300-8x`/`b300-4x` name hardware configurations rather than plan items, and no changelog prose or tracker reference appears in the changed units.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — §4 argues the gap is total ("no way to choose among a profile's topologies today") while `ModelProfile.gpu_variants` already selects a per-card-count configuration at launch, and the plan never reconciles the new axis with it.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §2 audits the store, §4 produces the launchers and their recipes, §6 performs the cutover; one deliverable each.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — `s3→s2`, `s4→rotate#s2,#s3`, `s5→s4`, `s6→s5,rotate#s5,serving-across-servers#s7` all resolve, and the `s6 → serving-across-servers#s7` edge is load-bearing and correctly declared: `_preferred_owner` (router.py:1639, called on the request path at router.py:1888) ranks by width, so without §7 both engines of `deepseek-v4.1-flash` would send every key to the B300 (the H200 idle) rather than sharing them.
